gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power the kit inverters draw when idle (the EG4 6000XP draws about 50 W, which is roughly 1.2 kWh a day or about 12% of the 10.2 kWh kit battery before any appliance runs), or that the rated surge figures can't be compared: EG4's 12,000 W claim lasts about 3.5 s and The Solar Lab measured 7.3–7.5 kW, SunGoldPower gives 13,000 VA with no duration, and ECO-WORTHY gives 6,000 W with no duration.
standout_why: I compared against the cited EnergySage page, the cited ecosolarkits.com guide, and preparedstates.com, which ranked first. None of the three states idle or no-load draw for any inverter. EnergySage lists continuous watts only and no surge figures. Ecosolarkits mixes 'peak VA' with 'surge W' and gives no durations. Preparedstates uses 'surge' and 'peak' without defining either and gives no durations. Ecosolarkits gives battery cycle counts without depth of discharge or end-of-life conditions. None of them works out what idle draw does to a battery's daily budget.
decides: The finding mostly changes how to size the kit. It only partly changes which kit to pick. On a 10.2 kWh kit like the EG4 6000XP package ChatGPT ranked first, about 12% of the battery goes to the inverter idling each day, so a cabin buyer should plan for about 1.2 kWh a day before any load. ChatGPT's surge ranking favours EG4 6000XP (12 kW), then SunGoldPower (13 kVA), then ECO-WORTHY (6 kW), but that ranking isn't sound: the units differ (W vs VA), no durations are given except EG4's, and EG4's measured surge was 7.3–7.5 kW. That makes the 3.5 kW ECO-WORTHY kit look weaker for well pumps than the headline numbers suggest, and it makes EG4 vs SunGoldPower a tie on what can actually be checked. One more fix: ECO-WORTHY's $2,499.99 1560W kit includes one 48V 100Ah (5.12 kWh) battery, which answers the 'confirm battery capacity' caveat ChatGPT left open.

findings.note: EG4's page gives only the best case, with PV connected (daytime). It gives no battery-only figure. 30 W × 24 h = 0.72 kWh/day.

findings.label: Idle draw, reviewer-checked
findings.source_title: EG4 6000XP Off-Grid Inverter Review – The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'it floated between 0.9 to 1.2 amps, which is right in line with the 50 watt idle listed in the specs.' The page names no reviewer and gives no date. My arithmetic: at 51.2 V nominal, 0.9–1.2 A = 46–61 W. 50 W × 24 h = 1.2 kWh/day = 11.7% of the 10.24 kWh battery in the EG4 6000XP kit ChatGPT showed (10.2 kWh).
